For each residue \(s \pmod{17}\), the number of unordered pairs \(\{x,y\}\subseteq \{1,\dots,17\}\) with
\[
x+y\equiv s \pmod{17}
\]
is \(\frac{17-1}{2}=8\), since only the diagonal \(x=y\) is excluded.

Any two distinct such pairs with the same sum are automatically disjoint. Thus for each residue \(s\), there are
\[
\binom{8}{2}=28
\]
ways to choose two disjoint pairs with sum \(s\).

There are \(17\) residues, so the number of good subsets is
\[
17\cdot 28 = 476.
\]
\[
\boxed{476}
\]
